activity.notes: Willie Seaweed (Kwaxitola/Hiłamas) was a high-ranking hereditary chief and major Kwakwaka'wakw artist from Blunden Harbour. Smithsonian and American Museum of Natural History records document him as chief and artist and emphasize his role in maintaining potlatch traditions during and after the Canadian prohibition. Because a precise accession date is not established, ATLAS begins the documented public chief-artist phase approximately around 1930, when surviving museum-documented works already identify him in that capacity.
